answer: Trust propagates from independently anchored identities through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, so influence depends on reachable, well-connected support rather than raw account count. A sybil cluster joined to honest nodes by a sparse external cut has low conductance; under normalized walk transitions, limited probability mass crosses that boundary, bounding its aggregate voting weight. A sonnet at the wharf may echo, but repetition alone adds no trusted edges.
